extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: An n-way parallel speech and text benchmark in 102 languages built on top of FLoRes-101, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It supports tasks including ASR, speech language identification, translation, and retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by starting from the FLoRes-101 sentence set, using its dev and devtest splits, re-splitting them into train/dev/test, then collecting three speech recordings per sentence from different native speakers with sex-balance targets. Additional workers validated whether recordings matched the input sentence, invalid recordings were discarded, and the final data were split with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Invalid recordings were discarded, leaving zero to three recordings per sentence; about 21.5% of sentences were missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated, and the authors planned to fill these gaps later.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source text came from FLoRes-101: 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated by human translators into 101 languages; the dataset used 2009 sentences from the dev and devtest splits. The raw speech data are native-speaker recordings of those sentences, kept as recorded from quiet or noisy environments at 16 kHz. Source transcripts were reused from the human-translated FLoRes transcripts, and the dataset provides raw, normalized, and character-based transcript versions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Speech recordings were validated by additional workers who checked whether each recording matched the input sentence; invalid recordings were discarded. The dataset also reused human-translated source transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation-based quality control was applied, with invalid recordings discarded; the paper reports that about 21.5% of sentences were missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings per sentence by three different native speakers; each recording was then evaluated by additional workers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Recording speakers were native speakers, with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset and resulting models are biased toward languages and regions with more pre-training data, with better performance on Western and Eastern European languages than on lower-resource regions. The paper also notes script-related and language-confusion biases, such as errors across mixed writing systems and confusion between acoustically similar languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The first version has incomplete coverage because many sentences are missing when no recordings were validated. The dataset is relatively small for training large models from scratch and is intended more for fine-tuning/evaluation. Performance is weaker for unseen languages and limited supervised data, and noisy recordings are retained without augmentation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, supporting broader multilingual and cross-modal speech research.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Sex ratio of speakers and speakers' native-speaker status were collected/used in data collection; geography is also used to group languages by region.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, fine-tuning, and evaluation/benchmarking across multiple speech tasks, including ASR, speech language identification, speech translation, and speech-text/speech-speech retrieval. The paper also provides tokenized transcript variants and states that the character-based version should be used for ASR.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly released via TFDS and Huggingface, and the authors plan future versions to fill missing recording gaps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Balanced speaker collection by sex ratio (at least 30/70% when possible) and creation of new train/dev/test splits from FLoRes dev and devtest with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test and a target ratio of 7:1:2.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid recordings were discarded; audio was kept as recorded without augmentation, sampled at 16 kHz, and segments were limited to 30 seconds. Text preprocessing included NFC then FST normalization, lowercasing, punctuation normalization/removal, and splitting words into characters with word-boundary tokens; raw, normalized, and character-based transcript versions were provided.

name.evidence: We introduce FLEURS, the Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech benchmark.

description.evidence: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.
